items.video_title: What is an Engine Misfire?
items.video_description: What is an Engine Misfire? Welcome to Mercie J auto care, where compassion and craftsmanship come together. I’m Rick Smith, master certified technician. So when your check engine light is on and you have a P03 series code so like a 301, 302, 306. That’s a misfire code and the 301 would be be cylinder, 306 would be cylinder 6, etc. So what does it take for a cylinder to fire? Well, you’re piston starts out of the top, your intake valve opens and like a syringe it sucks in air and fuel? Then the valves close, the piston comes up, compresses all that, when it gets to the top and it’s all nice and compressed, the spark plugs fires. This shoves the piston down just like if you’re pushing your leg down on a bicycle crank shaft and then after that, completes the firing process then the exhaust valve open, piston comes up and pushes it out of the tailpipe. So three things we have to have, one is that spark plug has to fire. So ignition coils, spark plugs and things like that need to make that happen. Two is we have to have fuel, so the fuel pump has to pump pressure, the injector has to squirt fuel into the cylinder. Third thing we have to have is that compression. So we could have anything like this 2012 Caravan that had a P0302. The exhaust valve is leaking, so we had low compression. We had to do a cylinder head. So you could need anything from the cylinder head to a major engine problem to a simple, spark plug, injector or even a vacuum leak. I hope this helps you understand a little bit more about what a misfire is with those P0 three… codes. Until next time so travels and blessings to you.

Additional context as this has gotten questions. On the back of the engine are the fuel injectors and in this video I am holding onto one of the connectors to the fuel injectors, causing the engine to run smooth. I took the connector out and spliced in a replacement. Upon inspection the wires inside of the connector were retracting and causing a loss of signal when going over bumps. In the video it begins as a misfire caused by that loss of signal. items.video_title: What is Engine Misfiring? Engine Misfire diagnostic and Troubleshooting
items.video_description:
Engine misfiring refers to a situation where one or more cylinders in an engine fail to fire properly. This means that the air-fuel mixture inside the cylinder does not ignite correctly, which can cause the engine to run unevenly. Misfires can lead to a variety of symptoms such as rough idling, loss of power, poor fuel efficiency, or even the engine stalling.

Common causes of engine misfires include:

Faulty spark plugs – These can wear out or become dirty, preventing a proper spark to ignite the fuel-air mixture.
Ignition system issues – Problems with components like ignition coils, wires, or the distributor can cause misfiring.
Fuel delivery problems – Clogged fuel injectors, a failing fuel pump, or a dirty fuel filter can restrict the proper flow of fuel.
Air intake problems – A clogged air filter or a malfunctioning mass airflow sensor can lead to an improper air-fuel mixture.
Engine compression issues – If the engine’s cylinders aren’t sealing properly due to worn piston rings or valve problems, it can lead to misfires.
Vacuum leaks – Leaks in the vacuum system can alter the air-fuel ratio and cause misfires.
To diagnose and fix a misfire, a mechanic will typically check for trouble codes using an OBD-II scanner, inspect the ignition system, and possibly test the fuel and air intake systems.

A healthy engine is smooth and consistent, but what does it sound and feel like when something is wrong? This video helps you identify the common signs of an engine misfire.

Listen and feel for these 3 symptoms:

1. Exhaust Sounds: Listen for sputtering, popping, or "coughing" noises from the exhaust pipe. It will sound uneven and rough.

2. Shaking & Vibrating: When the car is stopped or idling, does it shake or shudder like an out-of-sync washing machine?

3. Hesitation: When you press the gas pedal, does the car stumble or hesitate before accelerating smoothly?

If you notice any of these signs, especially if your Check Engine Light is on, it's a strong indicator of an engine misfire. Don't just guess the cause—use a diagnostic tool to read the specific fault code so you know exactly what needs to be fixed.

Injector ka kharab hona - Injector mein kharabi hone par, fuel ka sahi pravah nahi hota hai, jisse ki engine mein misfire ki sambhavna banti hai.

Ignition coil ki samasya - Ignition coil mein kharabi hone se, spark plug mein sahi tarah ki electrical current nahi jaati hai, jisse ki engine mein misfire ki sambhavna banti hai.

Compression loss - Engine ki compression loss bhi misfire ka ek karan ho sakta hai, jisme piston ya cylinder head mein kharabi ke karan compression loss hota hai.

In sabhi vajahon ki wajah se engine mein misfire ho sakta hai, isliye engine ki sahi dekhbhaal aur maintenance bahut mahatvapurn hoti hai.
